rootCauses.pluginIcons: Installer saved only iconUrl; widget always used network image provider.
rootCauses.animeCovers: MediaCover read CoverStore, but online SourceNetworkImage never wrote successful public covers.
rootCauses.spacePause: Input boundary handled arrows only, so blank video ignored space and focused controls owned activation.

behavior.installedArtwork: Persist bounded decoded PNG at trusted install; lazy existing-install backfill; local-first; retain old icon on image failure; uninstall package-specific cleanup.
behavior.coverCache: Reuse existing CoverStore only for original strict anonymous public Bangumi URL allowlist; client-specific in-flight identities remain distinct.
behavior.playback: Space keydown toggles once before controls; ignores editing/modifiers/modal/disabled; menu owns its keys and stable keyed controls preserve menu across disabling gestures.

windowsPlayer.keyDelivery: Flutter integration binding into production input; no OS keyboard hardware claim

sourceSecretScan.scope: Exact existing account values, encodings and packaged private/debug names; signing values only if locally available; not a complete vulnerability audit

actionableFindingsFixed: Sequential repository icon backfill held global installation lock: metadata-only repair plus visible-row byte backfill.
Mounted FileImage did not reload same-URL icon replacement: keyed remount and red-to-blue pixel regression.
Space intercepted settings-menu activation: menu disables playback input; keyed controls preserve active menu.
reviews.scope: Independent static image and keyboard reviewers; not a claim of no vulnerabilities.

iosIsolation.documentedTarget: 0.15.2, independent iOS189 acceptance work; checked again before normal release builds

limits: Flutter-delivered integration key events, not physical OS-keyboard input.
Actual native image widget rendering observed programmatically, no desktop pixel-inspection claim.
Standalone image smoke loaded real repository artwork with production image storage; it did not reinstall a third-party executable plugin.
Installation/update trust and failed-artwork lifecycle covered by isolated contract regressions.
Original user device data not touched.
Earlier failed/superseded targeted runs preserved; not counted as passing.
